note: Turkyilmaz et al. (2025) identified homozygous stop-gain p.(Arg526Ter) in SGSM3 in two siblings with nonsyndromic intellectual disability and short stature.

evidence.text: A homozygous stop-gain variant (c.1576C>T: p.(Arg526Ter)) in SGSM3 was identified in two siblings presenting with short stature and intellectual disability findings, supporting SGSM3 as a candidate for a nonsyndromic ID phenotype.

source.title: A Strong Candidate Gene for Nonsyndromic Intellectual Disability Phenotype: SGSM3
source.quote: In this study, a novel homozygous stop-gain (NM_015705.6: c.1576C>T: p.(Arg526Ter)) variation was detected in the SGSM3 gene in two siblings with short stature and ID findings.

evidence.text: Birnbaum et al. reported an intellectual disability syndrome associated with a homozygous frameshift founder variant in SGSM3 in Ashkenazi Jewish families who presented with delayed speech and mild to moderate intellectual disability.

source.title: Intellectual disability syndrome associated with a homozygous founder variant in SGSM3 in Ashkenazi Jews
source.quote: They all share a common homozygous frameshift variant in SGSM3, which segregated with the phenotype in … motor development yet delayed speech.
